text.p: BroadBand Technologies Inc on Wednesday denied that it infringes upon two patents held by a General Instrument Corp unit which relate to the transmission of digital video.
General Instrument's Next Level Communications unit last month filed the patent infringment and antitrust suit against BroadBand in San Francisco.
Next Level had asked for an injuction to prevent BroadBand from making, using or selling equipment that provides digital video signals.

Richard Jones, chief technology officer of BroadBand, said "General Instrument's patents pertain to video encoding and compression technology. These functions are not part of BroadBand's FLX 2500 switched digital broadband platform."
On March 18, Broadband filed a patent infringement suit against General Instrument in Raleigh, N.C.

The suit charged that General Instrument infringes BroadBand's patent for its switched digital broadband technology. The suit seeks to enjoin General Instrument from the manufacture, sale or use of equipment to provide switched digital broadband services.
